newsitem.title: USA: Hilton amends ITT lawsuit. [CORRECTED 22:12 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Hilton amends ITT lawsuit. [CORRECTED 22:12 GMT]

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp on Thursday said it amended its lawsuit against rival ITT Corp in a counter move to ITT's defense of selling assets to fend off Hilton's $6.5 billion hostile takeover bid for ITT.
In its lawsuit filed in the U.S. District Court in Las Vegas, Hilton challenges a change in control provision that is part of ITT's sale of five Sheraton hotels to FelCor Suite Hotels Inc.
The lawsuit also adds ITT's board members as defendants, and it seeks to bar ITT from selling any more assets without an open auction and without shareholder approval.
On Monday, ITT signed a definitive agreement to sell the hotels to FelCor for $200 million. Under the deal, ITT Sheraton, an ITT unit, would still manage the hotels.
But the agreement includes a stipulation giving FelCor the option to terminate the management contract if ITT is acquired.
Hilton claims that such provisions decrease the hotels' value, but ITT says they are standard procedure.
In a statement, Hilton said: "ITT's incumbent management is destroying a valuable corporate asset, the hotel management contracts with FelCor."
An ITT spokesman, however, defended the sale and change of control provision, saying everything the company has done has been in the interest of building value.

"Our FelCor deal is absolutely standard operating procedure for companies that operate hotels," said Jim Gallagher, spokesman for the New York-based hotel and gambling company. "FelCor had said it would not do the transaction if it did not have the change in control provision."
He declined to comment further on the specifics of the suit because the company has yet to be served.

Hilton launched its $55 per share takeover bid for ITT in late January, and ITT later rejected the offer as inadequate. ITT then began selling assets to focus on core businesses in hotels and gambling. Along with the Sheraton brand hotels, ITT owns the Caesars brand casinos.

But the FelCor deal, plus published reports that ITT has looked at offers for its upscale St. Regis hotel in New York and the Phoenician in Arizona, has Hilton concerned that ITT is selling core assets, too.
In its press release, Hilton called core asset sales "scorched earth" tactics.
ITT's Gallagher replied, "everything we have done has been done with the goal of building value for our shareholders."
In the past, ITT has said the hotels sold to FelCor were not part of the company's core strategy, and it has declined to discuss the published reports about the St. Regis and Phoenician.
Hilton's original suit, filed just after it launched the offer, seeks to dismantle ITT's so-called "poison-pill" takeover defense.

Today's amendments seek, among other things, to rescind the FelCor sale, to enjoin ITT from selling any further noncore or core assets and to bar ITT from selling assets without the approval of ITT shareholders.
